title: streaming: robust lifecycle controls for client cancel, disconnect, reconnect/resume and server timeouts (OpenAI-compat)
author: Maya Patel
description: Motivation: streaming clients (websocket and HTTP/1.1 chunked) were observed to leak server-side resources when clients sent explicit cancels, disconnected mid-stream, or attempted reconnect/resume across transient network failures. Additionally, the OpenAI compatibility layer did not expose consistent reconnect semantics which led to duplicated partial outputs and confusing errors for SDK users. This PR adds a cohesive set of streaming lifecycle controls: 1) explicit client Cancel handling that triggers an immediate soft-cancel path to release KV cache and batch slots while still allowing a short grace period for rollback/metrics emission, 2) robust disconnect detection with backpressure-aware server-side timeouts to avoid unbounded buffer growth, 3) reconnection and resume support for the OpenAI-compat streaming endpoint including idempotency tokens and resume cursors, 4) server-side timeout tuning and observability hooks so SRE can adjust SLO/timeout tradeoffs per route. Changes include protocol-level additions (Resume-Token header, X-Stream-Session for websockets), runtime lifecycle state machine updates, graceful cancellation flow in the serving runtime and a compatibility shim for SDKs that expect OpenAI-like reconnect semantics. Backwards compatibility: older clients that do not send resume tokens continue to get the previous behavior (no resume) and cancel still works as immediate termination. Rollout plan: staged rollout behind a feature flag shipping to canary hosts for 48 hours with expanded tracing, then gradual ramp across regions. Related: ENG-1789 for reconnect UX and SUP-3421 customer ticket describing duplicated partial events. Checklist: ensure unit + integration tests for resume/cancel flows, add e2e against python/ts SDKs, add metrics for canceled_by_client/reconnect_success/reconnect_resume_fail, feature flag + rollout docs. Impact: small server CPU increase on canary due to additional resume bookkeeping, measured and accounted in perf notes.
